maddy: heads up — I ran a long tail perf run on paged-attn with the new reserve/reclaim changes. seeing ~12% less tail latency but memory graphs look noisy
julian: nice! can you paste the trace?
maddy: pasted below — jumps when we hit a KV cache compaction event. sequence: active batches -> kernel fallback -> small allocs -> compaction sweep -> bigger pause
julian: hmm that sequence suggests reclaim is triggering during batch assembly, which fragments WS and forces kernel to pick smaller workspace kernels
kai: can you share the nvprof / nvtx span? also what env flags did you use to enable dynamic reserve?
maddy: nvtx snippet and flags
```
NVTX: span paged_attn_batch_start
NVTX: span kv_cache_probe
NVTX: span compact_sweep
flags: RW_WS_DYNAMIC=1 RW_RECLAIM_THRESHOLD=0.55 RW_COMPACT_TRIGGER_MS=6
```
sasha: 0.55 reclaim threshold is aggressive — we chatted about 0.7 earlier. dropping it could reduce compaction frequency but increase peak usage
julian: we need an experiment matrix: reclaim_threshold x compact_ms x reserve_target. small grid maybe 3x3x2. measure tail latency, OOM count, compaction time, and kernel-choice distribution
maddy: agreed. here's a quick perf command I ran to collect kernel-selection distribution
```
./perf_harness --workload=chat-mix --trace-kernels --kv=true --warmup=200 --iters=2000 --dump=/tmp/trace.json
jq -r '.events[] | select(.type=="kernel") | .name' /tmp/trace.json | sort | uniq -c
```
ops-bot: deployment staging/slot-3 finished rolling restart (tag: ws-reserve-expt) :white_check_mark:
julian: output shows spike in small-kernel invocations exactly at compaction events. that matches theory — compaction reduces contiguous workspace so runtime falls back to smaller kernel paths
kai: question: can we change reclaim policy to prefer freeing cold KV segments first instead of blanket compaction? maybe a lightweight LRU-preferential reclaim would keep WS contiguity for active batches
sasha: we have an eviction score per chunk already. the current compactor doesn't account for 'adjacent free regions' which causes fragmentation. we could tweak compaction to prefer coalescing nearby freed chunks rather than scattering reclaim across the heap
maddy: sketch of an approach:
- track adjacent-frees score per free-run
- when compacting, prefer runs that will produce longest contiguous region above reserve_target
- add a fast-path that delays compaction until batch ends if batch assembly is in-progress
julian: I like delaying compaction while batch assembly is hot — that should reduce kernel fallbacks. but we need a safe upper bound to avoid unbounded memory growth
ai: suggest metric: `batch_inflight_count` and `compaction_delay_ms = min( max_delay, batch_inflight_count * per_batch_delay_ms )`
kai: for experiments, propose matrix: reclaim_threshold in [0.6,0.7,0.8], compact_trigger_ms in [4,8,12], reserve_target in [0.15,0.25]
- run 2k iterations each, collect tail p99/p999, compaction count, kernel-fallback-rate, and OOMs
sasha: also add a variant that toggles 'prefer-coalesce' compactor flag on/off
maddy: schedule: I can run the grid on staging GPUs tonight, will post results tomorrow morning. any other metrics to capture?
julian: capture per-batch assembly latency histogram and KV probe latency. also record free-run-size histogram from allocator pre/post compaction
ops-bot: reminder: quota for staging GPUs between 02:00-06:00 UTC (low usage window)
maddy: ok kicking off jobs now. attaching the first run logs here — small improvement in p99, but compaction time increased ~18% when prefer-coalesce was enabled (likely heavier scanning)
kai: tradeoff expected. maybe we can make prefer-coalesce approximate — only scan limited window and stop early if found run >= desired_size
sasha: yes, a bounded scan fix sounds good. add a config param `coalesce_scan_budget` (ms or number of free-runs)
julian: if bounded scan reduces compaction cost while keeping contiguity, good win. otherwise consider a background defragmenter that runs at low priority between batches
maddy: noted. I'll run the second batch with coalesce_scan_budget=50 and post numbers
maddy: quick follow-up after 3 runs: 
- baseline reclaim=0.55: p99=87ms, p999=210ms, compactions=42, kernel-fallback-rate=7.4%
- prefer-coalesce (unbounded): p99=78ms, p999=195ms, compactions=39, compaction-ms total +18%
- prefer-coalesce (budget=50): p99=80ms, p999=198ms, compactions=40, compaction-ms +6%
julian: sweet — budgeted coalescing seems promising. next steps: put budgeted coalescer behind a feature flag and run longer soak with mixed workloads
sasha: and add monitoring for fragmentation: expose free-run-size percentiles and contiguous-max-size in console
kai: I'll prototype bounded-scanner tomorrow and wire a flag. can someone open an RFC for the allocator change so we can get design eyes on it?
maddy: opened draft RFC: https://go/repo/rfcs/allocator-coalesce-bounded — comments welcome
julian: thanks all. great iterative cycle. :tada:
ops-bot: scheduled job results uploaded: gs://staging-perf/2109876543/*
deploy-bot: feature flag ws.coalesce.budget enabled on staging
maddy: marking thread for follow-up after soak. tagging @sasha @kai for design review next week.
